objects.original: A finite-dimensional real Hilbert space with its Borel sigma-algebra, a Borel measure μ, real-valued smooth tests, the true gradient and a fixed real coefficient parameter C. Chewi's motivating objects are the Euclidean space and Langevin probability law π.
objects.reconstructed: E, μ, C and real tests v and f; A(g) is the square-entropy expression and D(g) is the squared Hilbert-gradient energy.
objects.evidence: The current module's scoped NormedAddCommGroup, real InnerProductSpace, CompleteSpace, MeasurableSpace and BorelSpace supply these objects; FiniteDimensional is local to the extension. Completeness is implicit in Hilbert space and automatic in finite dimension. Mathlib gradient is the Riesz image of the Fréchet derivative, which exists for every smooth test; it is not a freely specified vector field or a fallback value.

domains.original: Chewi §2.1.1 displays the genuine-integral inequality on C_c^∞(ℝ^d) for π and refers to a wider class by density without giving the domain here. The pinned ASTIS reconstruction uses a totalized premise on C_c^∞(E) for arbitrary μ and an explicit sufficient smooth L²/L²/L¹ conclusion domain.
domains.reconstructed: The universal premise is on C_c^∞(E); the conclusion is for smooth f in L²(μ) with ∇f in L²(μ;E) and h(f²) in L¹(μ).
domains.evidence: ContDiff ℝ ∞ is C-infinity and HasCompactSupport is compact support, not a C² test premise. Finite dimension is used for compact support of the radial cutoff, not for the shared limits. The candidate's separate description of the shared limit domain omits hypotheses; see the publication-only delta. This is not an error in the decoded extension domain.

quantifiers.original: Fix E, μ and C. If the inequality holds for every compact smooth v on this carrier, it holds for every eligible smooth f on the same carrier.
quantifiers.reconstructed: For each E, μ and C, a universal implication on v gives a universal implication on f with its three analytic hypotheses.
quantifiers.evidence: The elaborated Lean premise binds v under fixed μ and C, before introducing the arbitrary f. The proof substitutes each f_n into that premise. There is no exchange of universal and existential quantifiers, no cutoff-dependent C, and no probability, σ-finiteness or finiteness binder.

assumptions.original: The all-compact-smooth LSI at 2C and smoothness, f∈L²(μ), ∇f∈L²(μ;E), and f² log(f²)∈L¹(μ) for the target. No sign, nonzero mass, or extra measure hypothesis.
assumptions.reconstructed: Exactly these premises, with h(t)=t log t on t>0 and h(0)=0.
assumptions.evidence: MemLp with exponent 2 is a.e. strong measurability plus finite L² norm; its real square and vector squared-norm integrability consequences are used explicitly. Integrable for h(f²) is absolute integrability. None of these analytic binders is an unconditional assertion about all compact smooth tests for arbitrary μ. The lesson correctly derives integrability for the particular cutoff products from the envelopes.

conclusion.original: ∫h(f²) dμ − h(∫f² dμ) ≤ 2C ∫‖∇f‖² dμ with genuine integrable mass, entropy integrand and energy.
conclusion.reconstructed: A(f) ≤ 2C D(f) with the three integrands genuine on the stipulated domain.
conclusion.evidence: This is the same normalization and factor as Chewi's probability function form (Example 1.2.27). Lean establishes all three real integral limits, composes the mass limit with continuity of q log q, and takes the closed-order limit of the cutoff inequalities. The output is LSI, not a Poincaré inequality, KL Taylor expansion or maximal closed-domain extension.

scopes.original: Chewi's statement is classical for a probability law. ASTIS marks its arbitrary-measure totalized generalization and cutoff proof as a sufficient reconstruction, not a verbatim source theorem. Exercise 1.7 is a bounded downstream use.
scopes.reconstructed: A and D use the Bochner zero fallback only outside genuine integrability; h(0)=0 handles both zeros of f and zero mass.
scopes.evidence: Mathlib integral_undef confirms the fallback. On π, each compact smooth v and its gradient are bounded (the gradient vanishes off the closed support), so every premise integrand is integrable. Exercise 1.7 hints at the centered bounded compact g density 1+εg; for small ε, sqrt(1+εg) is smooth, bounded, and bounded away from zero, with bounded true gradient. It satisfies the analytic premises on π even when noncompact, so this result licenses its LSI application but does not prove the exercise. The lesson's source-scope label can be tightened as noted separately.

constant_dependencies.original: The same fixed C appears only in the factor 2C, independent of the target, compact test, and cutoff. No restriction on the sign of C is needed for the extension implication.
constant_dependencies.reconstructed: C∈ℝ is fixed in both A(v)≤2C D(v) and A(f)≤2C D(f).
constant_dependencies.evidence: The internal positive derivative-control constant K is distinct from C. Uniform bounds are χ∈[0,1], ‖Dχ_R‖≤K/R and R=n+1≥1. The proof uses continuity of multiplication by 2C and closedness of ≤, not an order-preserving multiplication step that would require C≥0.

deltas.description: Publication exposition only: candidate_publication_context.assumptions[2] says the cutoff-limit prerequisite 'by itself needs only C2 regularity and a complete real Hilbert/Borel carrier'. The preceding bullet names the analytic hypotheses for the extended LSI test, but the standalone prerequisite bullet omits them while claiming sufficiency. cutoff_integral_limits still requires MemLp f 2 μ, MemLp (gradient f) 2 μ, and Integrable (f² log(f²)) μ. On ℝ with Lebesgue measure and f≡1, f_n=χ_{n+1} has ∫f_n²≥2(n+1), while ∫f² totalizes to 0, so the first advertised limit fails on that literal domain. Say explicitly that the same L²/L²/L¹ conditions remain in force and that it is only the smoothness and ambient dimension requirements that are relaxed. No Lean or pinned-theorem repair is needed.

lesson.sources[0].scope says 'the sufficient density argument', which could suggest the cited pages give the cutoff proof. Printed p. 49 instead refers to density and omits the approximation; the main attribution correctly identifies the explicit argument as original ASTIS work. In the source label, use 'compact-test LSI and reference to extension by density'.

review_evidence: Independent comparison of the exact packet, live whole Lean module, anonymous reconstruction and authored publication context. Verified Sinho Chewi, Log-Concave Sampling, August 20, 2026, https://chewisinho.github.io/main.pdf (SHA-256 8818e8fb40c07bd70651bafe10e8ec4500197c836928330b90025ca47da52fae): PDF pp. 60–61 / printed pp. 48–49 give the compact C-infinity probability-law LSI and the density reference; PDF p. 55 / printed p. 43 gives the bounded Exercise 1.7 consumer; Example 1.2.27 fixes the entropy normalization. The complete current Lean module is byte-identical to the packet (SHA-256 25d865b9f731b83fa0af7fd32c183c2630c9fa86f5e36c4d8c1b4cddcd088cbc). Reviewed the private product, entropy and energy helpers and public limits: writing a=χ²∈[0,1], q=f², the envelopes are q, |q log q|+q and 2‖∇f‖²+2K²q; χ_{n+1} eventually equals 1 in a neighborhood of each x, so the genuine cutoff gradients are eventually equal pointwise. These bounds and measurability justify the three actual limits for the explicit analytic domain; finite dimension supplies the compact smooth test step only. The pinned ASTIS theorem, Lean and blind reconstruction agree, and their probability specialization correctly realizes the bounded source extension. The domain-mismatch verdict is for the current candidate publication wording of the shared prerequisite only, not for the pinned theorem or its proof. Recheck the publication binding after correcting that wording. No prior reviews or builds used.
